title: The Quantum Noise Fraction and the addressable fraction in High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Detection
summary: The quantum noise fraction $β$ -- the share of a detector's noise power that is quantum in origin -- bounds the sensitivity gain from any quantum technique at $\mathcal{E}_{\max}=1/\sqrt{1-β}$. In the kHz--GHz band the readout is a bosonic mode and $β=1/(2\bar{n}_{\rm th}+1+ν)$, so quantum noise dominates only below a thermal frontier $k_BT\ln 3=\hbarω$ (229 MHz at 10 mK) that governs mechanical resonators and electromagnetic cavities alike.
